gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Spindly and futuristic, Megrim looks like thread stitched along a path, with every stroke held to one hairline width. Noto Sans Samaritan reads sturdy and friendly.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-saurashtra: Wire-bent and angular, Megrim sketches its letters from a single length of line, sharp and a little futuristic. Noto Sans Saurashtra reads plainly beneath it.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-sc: Megrim's diagonals match its stems exactly, giving it a sharp, futuristic look. Noto Sans SC is the quieter one: its chalky sans-serif curves stay open and its ascenders hug the x-height, so it handles the reading while Megrim handles the attention.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Slim, sharp and futuristic, with one hairline stroke running through every letter. Noto Sans Sharada comes in heavier and bulkier, and its open curves keep a long stretch of text feeling clear.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Megrim's stems and arcs move in lockstep, one thin line throughout. Noto Sans Siddham has a large central band and an s with wide-hanging ends, so a size slightly bigger than usual would suit it.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through each line, with curve endings that keep their distance. gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height and wide, open curves. Megrim is best at being the thin, cut-ribbon headline with sharp angles, while the body font is best at carrying screen text in a plain sans.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Megrim draws like a technical drafting pen, steady and angular. Noto Sans Sundanese sits beneath with open-mouthed e crossbars and barely any gap between lowercase and capitals, so paragraphs run smooth and uninterrupted.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Futuristic and angular, Megrim looks like a skeleton outline given one fixed stroke thickness. Noto Sans Sunuwar follows with short ascender stems and curves that leave generous daylight, so text feels friendly page after page.
